We need to implement DP counting number of ways to represent n as sum of unique positive integers each raised to power x.

n up to 300, x up to 5. So compute list of possible values: v_i = i^x such that v_i <= n. Since i^x grows quickly; for x=5, i^5 <= 300 => i <= 300^(1/5) ~ 3.0? Actually 3^5 = 243; 4^5 = 1024 >300 so max i about 3. So total possible numbers limited. For x=2: sqrt(300)~17.32 => i up to 17.

Thus number of items small (<=~17). But we need to count subsets of these numbers whose sum equals n. This is classic subset sum counting with uniqueness constraint (each item can be used at most once). DP: dp[s] = number of ways to achieve sum s using processed items (each used at most once). Iterate over each value v, update dp from high to low: for s from n down to v: dp[s] = (dp[s] + dp[s-v]) % MOD. Initialize dp[0] = 1 (empty set). At end answer = dp[n].

Edge Cases: result may be zero.

Complexities: O(#items * n) time, O(n) memory.

Implementation details: compute list of powers. Use while loop: i=1; while True: p = i**x; if p > n: break; else append p; i+=1.

MOD=10**9+7.

Potential pitfalls: because numbers are unique and we iterate over items, DP ensures each used at most once.
